rows.meaning: Set once at creation. Neither party may change it.
Seller sets and may revise while `draft` or `published`.
Buyer chooses from a declared set. Resolves without assent.
Buyer sets a value within declared bounds. Resolves without assent.
Buyer provides data or an artifact.
Buyer may ask outside the declared space. Requires seller assent.
Computed. Neither party sets it directly.
Sub-fields carry different markers; see the section.

code_blocks.text:
Proposal          → the merchandising pitch, identity, lifecycle state and assent
Line Items[]      → fully self-contained buyable units, each in exactly one channel

exclusions_accepted:
  types:        [domain, app_bundle, iab_content_category, keyword]
  max_entries:  { domain: 5000, keyword: 500 }
  enforcement:  { domain: pre_serve, app_bundle: pre_serve,
                  iab_content_category: pre_serve, keyword: best_effort }
  verification: ["IAS", "DoubleVerify"]

exclusions:
  domain:           ["example-gambling.example"]
  app_bundle:       [{ platform: roku, bundle: "123456" }]
  iab_content_category: ["IAB-CT3.0:<id>"]   # IAB Content Taxonomy ids
  keyword:          ["crypto"]
  list_ref:         { url: "<url>", sha256: "<hash>" }

geo:
  available:  ["SGP", "THA", "IDN", "MYS"]
  included:   ["SGP", "THA"]
  pricing:    { "IDN": { delta_cpm: 18.00 }, "MYS": { delta_cpm: 21.00 } }
  max_select: 4

requires:
  all_of:  ["business-daily-display", "weather-app-ctv"]
  any_of:  []
  min_commitment:
    - { line_item_id: "business-daily-display", basis: spend, amount: 50000.00, currency: USD }

sentences.text: Custom proposal — built in response to a buyer's agent brief, referenced via `brief_ref`.
Each line item lands in the one its `transaction_mechanism` maps to:
A line item that declares `requires` (§ 5.6.3) may be committed only when its conditions are met.

`line_item_id` · `channel` · `environments.available[]` · `content_detail` · property names · `formats.included[]` · `pricing.cost_method` · `pricing.gross_rate` · `min_spend` · `addressable_scale` · `committed_metrics[]` · `transaction_mechanism` · `has_requires`
plus, from the parent proposal: `proposal_id` · `seller_name` · `description` · `valid_from` · `valid_until` · `linked_execution`.
`has_requires` is `true` when the line item declares `requires` (§ 5.6.3), so a screening agent does not recommend a line item that cannot be bought on its own.
Full Representation — every field, with all `catalog_ref` values resolved.
A `catalog_ref` is not inheritance.

Contents: `{ seller_id, generated_at, spec_version, proposals[] }`, where each entry in `proposals[]` carries `proposal_id`, `version`, the Summary Representation (§ 2.1) of each line item, and a `full_url` for the second phase.
Only standard proposals appear, and within them only line items whose `visibility` (§ 5.8) is `public`.
`registry_gated` and `named` line items do not.
Property lists stay as names in the summary; large lists use `catalog_ref` (§ 2.2).
Propose: fetch the Full Representation of shortlisted line items from `full_url`, then compose and commit as usual.
Only `requestable` fields require the counterparty to respond.
`audience_pricing` in earlier drafts was the precedent for this pattern — it expressed "if you change X, the price moves by Y".
`pricing` generalises it to every dimension a seller is willing to vary, and replaces it.
Each issued proposal has an independent `status`, `version` and `negotiation_history[]`.
Conditions are stated in AdCOM 1.0 terms: the distribution channel, the ad's media (`Placement` subtypes) and the device type.
Placement type, such as interstitial or rewarded (OpenRTB 2.6 `video.plcmt`, `imp.instl` and `imp.rwdd`), does not change the channel.
Impressions in linear TV, including addressable linear, are outside this table: they have no `channel` value in 3.0.
`apps[]` identifies the apps behind a property sold in `app_mobile` or `ctv`.
Keys follow the OpenRTB 2.6 `app` object where one exists.
Seller authorisation for an app is checked through `app-ads.txt` on its developer domain, not through the property's `domains`.
Keys follow AdCOM 1.0 `Placement` and its `DisplayPlacement`, `VideoPlacement` and `AudioPlacement` subtypes, and the matching OpenRTB 2.6 `Imp` attributes.
`plcmt`, `playmethod[]` and `api[]` take any code in List: Plcmt Subtypes - Video, List: Playback Methods and List: API Frameworks respectively.
`plcmt` takes its OpenRTB 2.6 name.
AdCOM 1.0 carries the same list as `VideoPlacement.ptype`.
OpenRTB 2.6 `Audio` has no `skip`, `skipafter` or `playbackmethod`, so for audio those keys map to AdCOM 1.0 `AudioPlacement` only.
An absent key does not constrain it: a line item that omits `instl` can deliver to interstitial and non-interstitial impressions alike.
AdCOM 1.0 reads an absent `reward` or `instl` as `0`; here it means either value.

An impression matches `api[]` when it supports every listed framework, `playmethod[]` when its playback method is one of the listed values, and `refresh` when the slot renders each creative for at least `min_interval_s` seconds before it refreshes, or does not refresh.
The presence of a URL in VAST `<ClickThrough>` does not establish that requesting it is safe for inspection.
Each targeting field except `time_zone`, `exclusions_accepted`, and `exclusions` declares bounds, not a value.
A bare value means the field is `seller-set`.
For `exclusions_accepted` and `exclusions`, the seller declares what it can enforce, and the buyer supplies its lists.
Each `app_bundle[]` entry is `{ platform, bundle }`.
`bundle` is the OpenRTB 2.6 `app.bundle` value; `platform` names the store (`ios` | `android` | `roku` | `fire_tv` | `samsung_tv` and other store platforms).
`iab_content_category[]` entries are IAB Content Taxonomy ids.
`enforcement` is `pre_serve` or `best_effort` per type.
`pricing` deltas add to `agreed_rate` as for any selectable field (§ 3.1).
A `daypart` window is `{ days[], start, end }`, with `days[]` from Monday to Sunday, `start` and `end` as HH:MM, and `end` exclusive, later than `start`, and allowed to be `24:00`.
`time_zone` names a zone in the IANA time zone database, such as America/New_York or UTC.
Like the calendar Day of OpenDirect 2.1 `Line.frequencyinterval`, `frequency_cap.period` is a calendar period in `time_zone`; weeks start on Monday.
Frozen when status becomes `agreed`.
An `idempotency_key` is opaque and scoped to one buyer and seller pair.
Transitions: `none` → `requested` → `held` → (`expired` | `released` | `converted`).
`converted` is terminal and occurs when the line item reaches `agreed`.
A bonus line item is a line item with `requires` and its own pricing, such as a discounted `gross_rate` or `cost_method: flat` at 0.
A conditional discount is modelled as a separate line item that `requires` unlocks, not as a price that changes according to the other line items selected.
If a line item referenced in `requires` becomes `sold_out` or `withdrawn` before commitment, the dependent line item becomes non-committable.
After `agreed`, cancellation of a referenced line item is governed by the dependent line item's `cancellation_policy`.
`exclusions` (§ 5.5) reveal the buyer's strategy.
OpenProposal supplies the agreed record, `terms_ref` and `correlation_id` a connector needs.
Runnable copies of every example below live in `examples/`.
See `examples/proposal.yaml`.
Shows `selectable` audiences with per-option pricing, a catalog reference, a buyer commitment, and `settable` bounds.
See `examples/line-item-display.yaml`.
Shows a buyer commitment naming the `proposal_id` and `version` it was priced against (§ 5.6.1).
See `examples/line-item-ctv.yaml`.
See `examples/line-item-audio.yaml`.
See `examples/line-item-ctv-bonus.yaml`.
The display line item is `registry_gated`, so it is not listed.
See `examples/manifest.json`.
Shows `placement` on in-app rewarded video, with OMID support that lets a buyer select a third-party `measurement_source`.
See `examples/line-item-rewarded-video.yaml`.
`description`, `specifications`, `best_for` and `seasonality_notes` are what a model needs to decide whether to look further.
Channel support cost one new field and one generalisation — `channel`, and `committed_metrics[]` as tuples — rather than a schema fork per channel.
Each has its own `proposal_id` per counterparty or destination, and may carry `proposal_template_id` (§ 4.1) to trace it back to its template.
Buyer-specific terms, such as annual rates and named visibility, live on the issued proposal's line items: `visibility: named`, `eligible_bidders[]` and their own `pricing[]`.
Buyer–seller relationships are expressed as issued proposals (`visibility: named`, `eligible_bidders[]` set to that buyer, with the negotiated `pricing[]`) plus the buyer agent's business rules.
`agreement_ref` and `terms_ref` (§ 5.10, § 5.8) point at the agreement and terms a line item is executed under; IO generation happens through connectors.
Do seller catalogs (`catalog_ref`) belong in 3.0, or should the object stay fully inline until a later version?
Once one line item guarantees `viewable_rate` and another `completion_rate`, there is no normalised way for a buying agent to compare or optimise across them.
The format registry has no entries for `audio/*`, `ctv/*` or `dooh/*`.
`specs` delegates to a registry that cannot currently answer for half the declared channels.
Is a `min_line_items` field needed on the proposal to require a bundle purchase, or is that left to buyer discretion?
Should `payment_terms` and `invoicing_party` be catalog references rather than repeated on every line item, given they are usually identical across a seller's shelf?
`environments[]` needs validation against real inventory.

statements.text: It is not a ratified IAB Tech Lab standard and MUST NOT be treated as one.
Each line item MUST be fully self-contained.
A field on a line item MUST NOT inherit its value from the proposal or from a sibling line item.
A buyer MAY select and commit a subset of a proposal's line items, unless the proposal sets `linked_execution` to `all` (§ 4.1).
A catalog response MAY return it.
It MUST contain, per line item:
`catalog_ref` values MUST remain unresolved in a summary.
A line item that carries `placement` (§ 5.2) MUST also give, in its summary, whichever of `placement.reward` · `placement.instl` · `placement.plcmt` · `placement.skip` it declares.
A full fetch MUST return it.
Any field whose value is drawn from a seller-maintained catalog MAY carry a reference in place of an inline value:
A field MUST carry either an inline value or a `catalog_ref`, never both.
References MUST be version-pinned.
A catalog entry MUST be immutable once referenced; a change creates a new version.
References MUST resolve during discovery.
When a proposal reaches status `agreed`, every `catalog_ref` MUST be replaced by its resolved value in the stored record, so the committed artifact is self-contained and immutable.
A seller MAY publish `https://<seller domain>/.well-known/openproposal.json`.
`ETag` / `Last-Modified` are REQUIRED, so buyers can poll cheaply.
Manifest entries MUST match the current version of each proposal.
The seller sets it and MAY revise it while status is `draft` or `published`.
Each option MAY carry a price delta.
The buyer MAY ask for a value outside the declared space.
`selectable`, `settable` and `supplied` fields MUST resolve without a round trip — everything needed to validate and price them is declared in the proposal.
An unset `selectable` or `settable` field takes its declared `included[]` or default, and that default MUST be explicit in the proposal.
Every field marked `selectable` MUST declare:
MAY be empty
A field marked `selectable` that carries a bare value and no `available[]` MUST be treated as `seller-set`.
Every field marked `settable` MUST declare its bounds: either `allowed[]` (an enumerated set) or `min` / `max` (a numeric or date range).
A field marked `settable` that carries a bare value and no bounds MUST be treated as `seller-set`.

Because audiences, properties, formats and, where it is selectable, `geo` are `selectable`, and buyer `exclusions` (§ 5.5) narrow delivery, `addressable_scale` and `availability` MUST be recomputed against the buyer's actual selection and exclusions.
OPTIONAL.
REQUIRED when `type` is `custom`
Entries MUST NOT be edited or removed
`proposal_template_id` MUST NOT be required for a buyer to transact.
REQUIRED.
The seller MUST serve a line item only on impressions of its `channel`.
A consumer MUST skip a line item whose `channel` it does not recognise, and MUST NOT reject the proposal because of it.
Each property MUST carry `domains`, `apps` or both
`plcmt` is REQUIRED for video ads.
Each `environments.available[]` value MUST match at least one impression to which 5.1.1 gives the line item's `channel`.
Each key takes an integer, except `playmethod[]` and `api[]`, which take arrays of integers, and `refresh`, an object whose `min_interval_s` is a REQUIRED integer.
The seller MUST NOT deliver the line item to an impression that does not match a key that is present.

Unless `api[]` includes OMID 1.0 (7), a line item whose `committed_metrics[]` includes `viewable_rate` and whose `environments.available[]` includes `app_mobile` or `ctv` SHOULD NOT offer a `measurement_source` vendor other than the seller.
A buyer MAY request a later date
An implementation performing inspection MUST NOT send any production notification.
An implementation MAY retrieve creative documents, follow VAST wrappers and inspect referenced media as needed for its checks.

The inspector MUST NOT request a destination or redirect that sends a production notification; it MAY use a separate inspection URL or the receiving service's documented test mode under the conditions below.
A preview that executes creative or verification code MUST prevent that code from sending production notifications.
Synthetic events MAY be sent to test endpoints, or through a test mode that the receiving service documents as excluding those events from production measurement and delivery diagnostics.
Inspection failures MUST be reported through diagnostics, without firing a production VAST `<Error>` or `verificationNotExecuted` URL.
An implementation MUST NOT report a check that was skipped or could not finish as passed.
`geo` MAY instead declare the selectable structure of § 3.1, so a line item can be priced by market.
REQUIRED with either
A seller MUST reject an entry whose platform it cannot determine, rather than apply it across stores.
A buyer MUST NOT supply an exclusion type absent from `exclusions_accepted.types`.
A seller MUST reject it deterministically rather than ignore it.
A seller MUST NOT present `best_effort` enforcement as a guarantee.
`list_ref` MUST be hash-pinned, and resolved into the stored record at `agreed`, as for `catalog_ref` (§ 2.2).
A seller whose rate differs by market MAY declare `geo` with the selectable structure of § 3.1:
A `geo` that declares `allowed[]` and no `available[]` MUST be treated as `settable` (§ 3.2).
A `geo` MUST NOT declare both.
OPTIONAL.
OPTIONAL.
The seller MUST NOT interpret it.

The seller MUST reject a new commitment attempt whose `version` is not the current version of the proposal named by `proposal_id`, whose proposal is past `valid_until`, or whose `pricing[].price_valid_until` has passed.
The rejection MUST return the current version number, so the buyer can fetch it again.
These checks MUST be deterministic, as for `idempotency_key`.

For a replay from the same buyer of a commitment attempt the seller has already processed, with the same `idempotency_key` and the same commitment terms, the seller MUST return the original result and MUST NOT create a second commitment.
Reusing an `idempotency_key` with different commitment terms MUST produce an explicit conflict and MUST NOT create or modify a commitment.
Line items that MUST all be in the same commitment
Line items of which at least one MUST be in the same commitment
References in `requires` MUST point to line items in the same proposal and version.
A seller MUST reject a commitment that includes a line item whose `requires` is unmet.
This check MUST be deterministic.
A seller MUST reject a proposal at publication if `requires` references form a cycle.
Seller declares a ceiling; a buyer MAY request above it
OPTIONAL; REQUIRED when `terms_acceptance_required` is `true`.
`terms_ref` MUST be hash-pinned and frozen at `agreed`.
A seller MUST NOT disclose a buyer's `exclusions` to any party other than that buyer.
A seller MAY offer the same inventory through more than one
